data.title: mTOR inhibits autophagy by controlling ULK1 ubiquitylation, self-association and function through AMBRA1 and TRAF6
data.authors: Nazio F; Strappazzon F; Antonioli M; Bielli P; Cianfanelli V; Bordi M; Gretzmeier C; Dengjel J; Piacentini M; Fimia GM; Cecconi F

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTOR restrains autophagy by controlling ULK1 ubiquitylation and stability via AMBRA1/TRAF6.
data.abstract_excerpt: Autophagy is important in the basal or stress-induced clearance of bulk cytosol, damaged organelles, pathogens and selected proteins by specific vesicles, the autophagosomes. Following mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) inhibition, autophagosome formation is primed by the ULK1 and the beclin-1-Vps34-AMBRA1 complexes, which are linked together by a scaffold platform, the exocyst. Although several regulative steps have been described along this pathway, few targets of mTOR are known, and the cross-talk between ULK1 and beclin 1 complexes is still not fully understood.
